intent.raw_query: New Zealand South Island, $4000, hiking and bungee jumping, November 2026

selected_hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, New Zealand South Island

experiences.name: Nevis Bungy Jump
experiences.description: Take the ultimate leap from New Zealand's highest bungy jump at 134 meters above the Nevis River gorge. This iconic AJ Hackett experience offers breathtaking views of the Remarkables mountain range and an adrenaline rush like no other. The jump includes a scenic gondola ride to the suspended pod over the gorge.

experiences.name: Routeburn Track Great Walk
experiences.description: Hike one of New Zealand's nine Great Walks through stunning alpine scenery connecting Fiordland and Mount Aspiring National Parks. The 32km trail features dramatic mountain passes, glacial lakes, and ancient beech forests. Day hikers can tackle the Routeburn Falls section for spectacular views without requiring a multi-day commitment.

experiences.name: Milford Sound Kayak and Hike Combo
experiences.description: Combine a guided sea kayak paddle through the majestic Milford Sound fiord with a short hike along the Milford foreshore track. Paddle beneath towering 1200-meter cliffs, spot fur seals and dolphins, and witness cascading waterfalls up close. This guided full-day experience blends water adventure with light hiking in one of the world's most dramatic landscapes.

experiences.name: Franz Josef Glacier Valley Walk
experiences.description: Hike through a dramatic glacial valley to the terminal face of the Franz Josef Glacier, one of the world's most accessible glaciers. The self-guided valley floor walk winds through ancient rainforest and glacial moraine with interpretive signs explaining the glacier's rapid retreat. For a more immersive experience, join a guided heli-hike to walk on the glacier's icy surface.

experiences.name: Queenstown Ledge Bungy and Swing
experiences.description: Experience the original Kawarau Bridge Bungy, the world's first commercial bungy jump site, where AJ Hackett launched the sport in 1988. Jump 43 meters above the turquoise Kawarau River and optionally get dunked in the water below. The historic site includes a free museum and viewing platform, making it a cultural landmark as well as a thrilling activity.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - New Zealand South Island
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled - flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled - flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Christchurch or Queenstown airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. Collect luggage, clear customs, and arrange budget transfer or shuttle to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and get a good night's rest to recover from travel.

meals.breakfast: On the plane
meals.lunch: On the plane or at airport
meals.dinner: Grab a quick bite at the airport arrivals hall or a 24-hour petrol station convenience store near your accommodation - keep it simple tonight

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book an airport shuttle in advance to save money vs taxis. Download offline maps (Maps.me or Google Maps offline) before landing. Exchange a small amount of NZD cash at the airport for convenience. Keep receipts for budget tracking.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from jet lag. After a late breakfast, explore the immediate beachfront area around Aegean Bliss Resort on foot. Take a leisurely walk along the beach, breathe in the fresh South Island air, and get oriented with your surroundings. Visit a local supermarket (Countdown or Pak'nSave) to stock up on budget groceries, snacks, and water bottles for the trip ahead.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the nearest town centre for a self-guided walking tour. Explore local parks, waterfront areas, and free public spaces. Check out any free museums or galleries nearby. Visit the local i-SITE visitor information centre to pick up free maps, confirm bookings, and get insider tips on free activities in the region.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll back along the beachfront at sunset for stunning South Island coastal views. Plan and review your itinerary for the next 12 days. Organise your hiking gear and check that all equipment is ready for upcoming Great Walks.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at accommodation - pick up bread, eggs, and fruit from supermarket (NZD $10-15 for supplies)
meals.lunch: Supermarket deli sandwich or pie from a local bakery (NZD $5-8)
meals.dinner: Cook a simple pasta or rice meal in the hostel/resort kitchen using supermarket ingredients (NZD $8-12)

day_by_day.notes: New Zealand supermarkets like Pak'nSave are the most budget-friendly. Stock up on oats, bread, peanut butter, canned goods, and fresh fruit to keep daily food costs under NZD $20. Check if your accommodation has a kitchen available.

day_by_day.morning: Early start - depart for Franz Josef township. If travelling by budget bus (InterCity or Naked Bus), book in advance for best fares. En route, stop at any free scenic lookouts. Arrive in the Franz Josef/Westland Tai Poutini National Park area by late morning. Check in to a budget hostel or campground in Franz Josef village.
day_by_day.afternoon: Franz Josef Glacier Valley Walk - Hike through the dramatic glacial valley to the terminal face of Franz Josef Glacier. This iconic DOC (Department of Conservation) walk is completely FREE and takes approximately 2-3 hours return. Walk through ancient rainforest, cross braided riverbeds, and get up close to one of the world's most accessible glaciers. The scenery is breathtaking with towering ice walls and surrounding peaks.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Franz Josef village. Visit the free DOC visitor centre to learn about the glacier's history and climate change impact. Watch the sunset paint the glacier and surrounding Alps in golden light from the village lookout point.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered oats or toast at accommodation before departure (NZD $3-5)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from supermarket - sandwiches, fruit, and snacks eaten at glacier viewpoint (NZD $8-10)
meals.dinner: Cook at hostel kitchen or grab a budget meal at a local takeaway in Franz Josef village (NZD $12-18)

day_by_day.notes: The Franz Josef Glacier Valley Walk is FREE via DOC. Wear sturdy shoes and bring waterproof layers as West Coast weather changes rapidly. Do NOT venture beyond the marked safety barriers - the glacier is active and dangerous. Bring plenty of water and snacks. Sandflies are notorious on the West Coast - bring insect repellent!

day_by_day.morning: Optional: Rise early for a second visit to Franz Josef Glacier at dawn for incredible morning light photography (free). Alternatively, explore the free Waiho River Walk or Peter's Pool Walk near Franz Josef - both are short, scenic DOC tracks through temperate rainforest with stunning glacier views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Travel south along the spectacular West Coast to Fox Glacier township. Stop at free scenic lookouts including Lake Matheson (the famous 'mirror lake' reflecting Aoraki/Mt Cook - free entry, small parking fee). Walk the Lake Matheson Reflection Walk (approximately 1.5 hours, free) for iconic South Island scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Settle into budget accommodation in Fox Glacier or continue driving toward Haast Pass. Enjoy the dramatic coastal and mountain scenery as you travel. If staying in Fox, take a short evening walk to Fox Glacier viewpoint (free).

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at hostel - oats with banana (NZD $3-5)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch enjoyed at Lake Matheson picnic area (NZD $8-10)
meals.dinner: Cook at hostel kitchen or budget takeaway - fish and chips from a local shop is a classic NZ budget meal (NZD $10-15)

day_by_day.notes: Lake Matheson is best visited in the early morning for perfect reflections before the wind picks up. The drive from Franz Josef to Fox Glacier is only 25km but allow extra time for photo stops. Check road conditions at nzta.govt.nz as West Coast roads can be affected by weather and slips.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early and drive the stunning Haast Pass (SH6) - one of New Zealand's most scenic drives, passing through UNESCO World Heritage rainforest, waterfalls, and dramatic gorges. Stop at free DOC viewpoints: Thunder Creek Falls (a 10-minute walk to a 28m waterfall), Fantail Falls, and the Gates of Haast bridge. All stops are free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Wanaka by early afternoon. Drop bags at budget accommodation (Wanaka has several excellent backpacker hostels). Walk to the famous 'That Wanaka Tree' - the iconic lone willow tree in Lake Wanaka (free). Stroll along the Wanaka lakefront, enjoy the mountain views, and explore the charming township on foot.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset over Lake Wanaka and the surrounding mountains from the lakefront - one of the most beautiful free experiences in New Zealand. Browse local restaurants for budget options or cook at the hostel.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered before departure (NZD $3-5)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at a waterfall stop along Haast Pass (NZD $8-10)
meals.dinner: Budget meal in Wanaka - try a local bakery, supermarket hot food counter, or affordable cafe (NZD $12-18)

day_by_day.notes: Fill up on petrol before leaving Franz Josef/Fox area as there are limited fuel stops along Haast Pass. The drive from Fox Glacier to Wanaka is approximately 3-4 hours including stops. Wanaka has a Countdown supermarket - stock up on supplies here as it's cheaper than smaller towns ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Hike the Roy's Peak Track from Wanaka - one of the most iconic hikes in New Zealand with panoramic views of Lake Wanaka, Mt Aspiring, and surrounding Alps. The track is 16km return with 1,200m elevation gain and takes 5-6 hours. Start early (6-7am) to avoid crowds and afternoon heat. This hike is completely FREE.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Roy's Peak hike and reach the famous summit viewpoint. The view is absolutely spectacular - a must-do for hikers. Take your time at the top before descending. The descent takes approximately 2-3 hours.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Wanaka tired but exhilarated. Soak tired legs in the cool waters of Lake Wanaka (free natural spa!). Enjoy a well-deserved dinner in town. Rest up for more adventures ahead.

meals.breakfast: Early self-catered breakfast before the hike - oats, banana, and coffee (NZD $3-5)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch at the Roy's Peak summit - sandwiches, nuts, chocolate, and plenty of water (NZD $8-10)
meals.dinner: Treat yourself to a slightly more substantial meal after the big hike - try a local pub or affordable restaurant in Wanaka (NZD $15-22)

day_by_day.notes: Roy's Peak is a challenging but rewarding hike - bring 2-3 litres of water per person as there is no water on the track. Sunscreen and a hat are essential in November (NZ summer). The track can be crowded on weekends - starting at dawn helps. Wear proper hiking boots. Check weather forecast at metservice.com before heading out.

day_by_day.morning: Rest morning after yesterday's big hike. Sleep in and enjoy a slow breakfast. Visit the free Wanaka Outlet walking track along the lake edge. Explore the Wanaka township, browse local markets (Saturday markets often run in summer), and visit the free public library or DOC office to plan ahead.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive or take a shuttle to Queenstown (approximately 1 hour from Wanaka). Check in to budget accommodation in Queenstown - the adventure capital of the world. Walk the Queenstown waterfront along Lake Wakatipu and take in views of The Remarkables mountain range. Explore the lively town centre.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Queenstown's vibrant atmosphere. Walk up to the free Bob's Peak viewpoint via the Tiki Trail (free hiking track, 45 minutes up) for incredible panoramic views over Queenstown and Lake Wakatipu at sunset - far cheaper than the Skyline Gondola.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at Wanaka hostel (NZD $3-5)
meals.lunch: Grab a cheap eat in Wanaka before departing - bakery pie or supermarket sandwich (NZD $5-8)
meals.dinner: Queenstown has many budget options - try Fergburger (iconic NZ burger, NZD $12-16), Vudu Cafe, or supermarket meal prep (NZD $10-18)

day_by_day.notes: Queenstown is the most expensive town in the South Island - budget carefully here. Cook your own meals as much as possible. The Tiki Trail to Bob's Peak is free vs NZD $36+ for the gondola. Book bungee jumping well in advance online for the best prices - AJ Hackett Bungy offers better rates when booked online.

day_by_day.morning: BUNGEE JUMPING DAY! Head to AJ Hackett Kawarau Bridge Bungy - the world's first commercial bungee jumping site (1988). The Kawarau Bridge jump is 43 metres above the stunning turquoise Kawarau River. Book online in advance for best rates (approximately NZD $165-195). This is a once-in-a-lifetime experience! Arrive early for your session.
day_by_day.afternoon: Adrenaline still pumping! Walk the free Kawarau Gorge Suspension Bridge area and enjoy the stunning scenery. Drive or shuttle back to Queenstown. Explore the free Queenstown Gardens on the peninsula - beautiful lakeside park with rose gardens and disc golf course.
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate your bungee jump! Watch the sunset over Lake Wakatipu from the waterfront. Share your experience with fellow travellers at the hostel. Browse the Queenstown night market (if running on Sundays in November) for affordable street food options.

meals.breakfast: Light self-catered breakfast before the jump - don't eat too heavily! (NZD $3-5)
meals.lunch: Pack a lunch to eat after the jump at Kawarau Gorge or grab a pie from a local bakery (NZD $8-12)
meals.dinner: Budget celebration dinner - Fergburger, a local pub meal, or cook at the hostel (NZD $12-18)

day_by_day.notes: Kawarau Bridge Bungy is the most affordable and iconic of Queenstown's bungee options. Book well in advance online for the best price. Wear comfortable, secure clothing. Remove loose items (glasses, jewellery) before jumping. The experience includes a video/photo package for an additional cost - decide in advance if you want this memento. Weight restrictions apply - check AJ Hackett website.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Queenstown early for Te Anau - the gateway to Fiordland National Park (approximately 2 hours drive or InterCity bus). Arrive in Te Anau and check in to budget accommodation. Visit the free DOC Fiordland National Park Visitor Centre to learn about the park and confirm Routeburn Track arrangements.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Te Anau township and the beautiful Lake Te Anau waterfront (free). Walk the free Lake Te Anau Lakefront Track. If budget allows, consider a short cruise on Lake Te Anau to visit the Te Ana-au Glowworm Caves (approximately NZD $55-75 - a worthwhile splurge if budget permits). Alternatively, enjoy the free lakefront views and birdwatching.
day_by_day.evening: Prepare and pack your gear for the Routeburn Track Great Walk starting tomorrow. Organise food supplies - purchase all food from Te Anau supermarket as it's the last major shopping stop. Pack lightweight, calorie-dense hiking food. Attend the free DOC briefing if available.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered on the road (NZD $3-5)
meals.lunch: Te Anau bakery or supermarket (NZD $8-10)
meals.dinner: Cook at hostel - carb-load for the Great Walk tomorrow! Pasta, rice, or noodles (NZD $8-12)

day_by_day.notes: IMPORTANT: Routeburn Track hut passes must be booked in advance through DOC (doc.govt.nz). Great Walk hut passes cost approximately NZD $65-75 per night per person in peak season (November is peak). Book months in advance as the Routeburn sells out quickly. Confirm your booking and print/download your passes. Pack all food for 3 days on the track.

day_by_day.morning: ROUTEBURN TRACK - DAY 1. Arrange early shuttle from Te Anau or Queenstown to the Routeburn Shelter trailhead (The Divide on SH94). Shuttles run by Tracknet or similar operators (approximately NZD $25-40 one way). Begin hiking the Routeburn Track - one of New Zealand's nine Great Walks. Start at The Divide and hike to Lake Howden Hut (approximately 1 hour, easy warm-up section through beautiful beech forest).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue from Lake Howden Hut toward Routeburn Falls Hut. The trail climbs through stunning beech forest with views opening up to alpine meadows, cascading waterfalls, and dramatic mountain scenery. This section is approximately 12km with significant elevation gain. Marvel at Earland Falls (174m high) along the way.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Routeburn Falls Hut (1,000m elevation). Enjoy the spectacular alpine views. Cook dinner using your packed hiking food in the hut kitchen. Socialise with fellow trampers from around the world. Watch the alpenglow on the surrounding peaks. Sleep in DOC hut bunks.

meals.breakfast: Early self-catered at Te Anau hostel before shuttle departure (NZD $3-5)
meals.lunch: Trail snacks and packed lunch eaten on the track - energy bars, nuts, dried fruit, crackers (NZD $5-8 pre-purchased)
meals.dinner: Packed hiking meal cooked at hut - dehydrated meal, instant noodles with tuna, or similar lightweight option (NZD $8-15 pre-purchased)

day_by_day.notes: Routeburn Track hut fee approximately NZD $65-75/night (pre-booked). Total distance Day 1: approximately 13km. Elevation gain: significant. Difficulty: Moderate-Hard. Wear proper hiking boots with ankle support. Bring waterproof jacket and warm layers - alpine weather can change suddenly. Huts have gas cookers, running water, and flush toilets. No camping on Great Walks without a campsite pass.

day_by_day.morning: ROUTEBURN TRACK - DAY 2. Rise early and enjoy the sunrise over the alpine landscape from Routeburn Falls Hut. After breakfast, hike up to the spectacular Routeburn Flats and continue to Harris Saddle (1,255m) - the highest point of the track. On a clear day, the panoramic views from Harris Saddle are absolutely breathtaking - stretching across Fiordland and the Darran Mountains.
day_by_day.afternoon: Optional side trip from Harris Saddle: Hike to Conical Hill (additional 1 hour return, highly recommended for even more spectacular 360-degree views). Continue descending through stunning alpine scenery toward Mackenzie Hut. Pass through open tussock grasslands with views of the Hollyford Valley below.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Lake Mackenzie Hut - arguably the most beautiful hut location on the track, perched beside the stunning turquoise Lake Mackenzie surrounded by towering peaks. If weather permits, take a refreshing (very cold!) swim in the lake. Cook dinner and enjoy the incredible surroundings. Watch the stars emerge over the mountains.

meals.breakfast: Packed hiking breakfast at hut - instant oats, coffee, dried fruit (NZD $5-8 pre-purchased)
meals.lunch: Trail lunch eaten at Harris Saddle or Conical Hill with incredible views (NZD $5-8 pre-purchased)
meals.dinner: Hut kitchen meal - dehydrated meal or packaged hiking food (NZD $8-15 pre-purchased)

day_by_day.notes: Routeburn Track hut fee approximately NZD $65-75/night (pre-booked). Total distance Day 2: approximately 11km. This is the most spectacular day on the track - clear weather makes it truly world-class. If weather is poor at Harris Saddle, do NOT attempt Conical Hill. Check with DOC wardens at the hut about conditions. The track can be icy in early morning even in November.

day_by_day.morning: ROUTEBURN TRACK - DAY 3. Final day on the Great Walk. Wake up to stunning views over Lake Mackenzie. After breakfast, pack up and begin the final section of the Routeburn Track descending toward the Routeburn Shelter at the Glenorchy end. Hike through ancient beech forest with glimpses of the Dart River valley below.
day_by_day.afternoon: Complete the Routeburn Track at the Routeburn Shelter trailhead near Glenorchy. Celebrate finishing one of New Zealand's greatest walks! Arrange pre-booked shuttle from Routeburn Shelter to Glenorchy or Queenstown (book with Tracknet in advance, approximately NZD $25-45). Arrive in Queenstown or Glenorchy by afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Queenstown for the night. Check in to budget accommodation. Enjoy a hot shower - the best shower of your life after 3 days on the track! Do laundry. Celebrate completing the Routeburn Track with a well-deserved meal in Queenstown.

meals.breakfast: Final packed hiking breakfast at Lake Mackenzie Hut (NZD $5-8 pre-purchased)
meals.lunch: Last trail lunch on the track or grab food in Glenorchy if time permits (NZD $8-12)
meals.dinner: Celebration dinner in Queenstown - you've earned it! Budget pub meal or Fergburger (NZD $15-22)

day_by_day.notes: Total Routeburn Track: approximately 32km over 3 days. Book your return shuttle from Routeburn Shelter (Glenorchy end) in advance as services are limited. Glenorchy is a beautiful small town worth a brief explore if your shuttle timing allows. Consider stopping at Glenorchy Lagoon for a short walk and stunning views of the Dart River and surrounding peaks.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Queenstown and the South Island. Sleep in or rise early for one last free activity - walk the Queenstown Hill Time Walk (Te Tapu-nui, approximately 2 hours return, free) for panoramic final views over Queenstown, Lake Wakatipu, and The Remarkables. A perfect farewell to the South Island's stunning landscapes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to accommodation, collect bags, and check out. Visit any last-minute spots in Queenstown - the lakefront, Queenstown Gardens, or browse the town centre. Head to the airport for your departure flight. Allow plenty of time for check-in and security.
day_by_day.evening: Depart from Queenstown Airport or transfer to Christchurch for onward travel. Reflect on an incredible 13-day adventure across the South Island - glaciers, Great Walks, bungee jumping, and breathtaking scenery. New Zealand South Island will have left an indelible mark!

meals.breakfast: Final self-catered breakfast or treat yourself to a cafe breakfast as a farewell (NZD $5-15)
meals.lunch: Light lunch from a supermarket or bakery before heading to airport (NZD $8-12)
meals.dinner: Airport meal or on the plane

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2 hours before your flight for airport check-in and security at Queenstown Airport. The airport is small but can get busy. Return any rental car with a full tank of petrol to avoid surcharges. Do a final budget review - a well-planned 13-day South Island trip on a budget should total approximately NZD $1,800-2,400 per person including accommodation, transport, food, Routeburn hut fees, and the bungee jump. The Routeburn Track hut fees (NZD $130-150 for 2 nights) and Kawarau Bungy (NZD $165-195) are the biggest single expenses - plan accordingly.

day_by_day.morning: No activities - flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities - flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Christchurch or Queenstown airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. Collect luggage, arrange transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in and settle into your Beachfront accommodation. Light refreshments at the hotel bar if available.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport
meals.dinner: Grab a quick bite at the airport arrivals hall or a late-night cafe near the resort upon arrival

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — you will arrive late at night. Confirm transfer arrangements in advance. Have NZD cash or a card ready for any immediate expenses. Rest is the priority tonight.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. After a leisurely breakfast, take a gentle orientation walk along the beachfront near Aegean Bliss Resort to get your bearings. Explore the local area and any nearby coastal trails on foot.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the nearest town centre for a self-guided walking tour. Browse local shops, pick up any hiking supplies or gear you may need, and visit a local visitor information centre to confirm upcoming bookings and activity schedules.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed dinner at a waterfront restaurant near the resort. Enjoy a glass of New Zealand Sauvignon Blanc and plan the days ahead. Early night to recover from jet lag.

meals.breakfast: Buffet breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort or a local cafe — try eggs benedict and flat white coffee
meals.lunch: Casual cafe lunch in town — try a classic Kiwi meat pie or fish and chips
meals.dinner: Mid-range waterfront restaurant near the resort — grilled New Zealand salmon or lamb rack, NZD 35-55 per person

day_by_day.notes: Use this day to acclimatise, adjust to the time zone, and stock up on essentials like sunscreen, insect repellent, and a refillable water bottle. Check weather forecasts for the week ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Drive or transfer to Franz Josef township (if basing near the West Coast) or arrange a day trip. Begin the Franz Josef Glacier Valley Walk — a guided hike through a dramatic glacial valley leading to the terminal face of the Franz Josef Glacier. Depart early to beat crowds and enjoy cooler morning temperatures.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the glacier valley hike, taking in the ancient blue ice formations, glacial streams, and surrounding rainforest. The full valley walk typically takes 3-4 hours return. Return to the trailhead and visit the DOC visitor centre to learn about the glacier's history and climate change impact.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Franz Josef village. Freshen up and enjoy dinner at a local restaurant. Debrief the day's hike over a hearty meal.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort or pack a packed lunch from a local bakery before departing
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or snacks on the trail — energy bars, sandwiches, fruit
meals.dinner: The Landing Bar & Restaurant in Franz Josef village — wood-fired pizza or venison burger, NZD 25-40 per person

day_by_day.notes: Wear sturdy hiking boots and layered clothing as glacier areas can be cold and wet even in November. The valley walk is accessible without crampons but check DOC conditions before departure. Book guided glacier hike in advance if preferred.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Franz Josef and drive south along the spectacular West Coast highway toward Wanaka or Queenstown. Stop at Lake Matheson for the famous mirror lake reflection walk — a 1.5-hour loop trail through kahikatea forest with stunning views of Aoraki Mount Cook.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the scenic drive south. Stop at Haast Pass lookout and walk the short Thunder Creek Falls track (10 minutes return) to a stunning 28-metre waterfall. Arrive in Wanaka by mid-afternoon. Check out the lakefront and take a stroll along Wanaka waterfront promenade.
day_by_day.evening: Settle into Wanaka or continue to Queenstown. Enjoy dinner at a lakeside restaurant with views over Lake Wanaka or Lake Wakatipu.

meals.breakfast: Cafe breakfast in Franz Josef before departing — eggs on toast and coffee
meals.lunch: Roadside stop or picnic lunch at Haast Pass — pack supplies from a supermarket
meals.dinner: Ritual Cafe & Bar in Wanaka or Fergburger in Queenstown (iconic Kiwi burger joint) — NZD 20-35 per person

day_by_day.notes: The drive from Franz Josef to Queenstown is approximately 4.5-5 hours with stops. Fill up on petrol before leaving Franz Josef as stations are sparse along the West Coast. November daylight extends to around 9pm, giving plenty of driving light.

day_by_day.morning: Head to Queenstown for the Queenstown Ledge Bungy and Swing experience. Start with the iconic Kawarau Bridge Bungy — the world's first commercial bungy jump site, a 43-metre plunge above the turquoise Kawarau River. Watch other jumpers, then take your leap. The atmosphere is electric and the setting is breathtaking.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the adrenaline rush, explore the Kawarau Bridge area and browse the AJ Hackett bungy experience centre. Head back into Queenstown and take the Skyline Gondola up Bob's Peak for panoramic views of the Remarkables mountain range and Lake Wakatipu. Try the luge if time permits.
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate your bungy jump with a well-earned dinner in downtown Queenstown. Queenstown's vibrant nightlife offers plenty of mid-range dining options. Explore the lakefront and Steamer Wharf precinct.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a Queenstown cafe — try Vudu Cafe & Larder for excellent coffee and eggs
meals.lunch: Casual lunch at Skyline Gondola restaurant or a quick bite in town — NZD 20-30
meals.dinner: Rata Restaurant or The Bunker in Queenstown — New Zealand cuisine with local produce, NZD 40-60 per person

day_by_day.notes: Book the Kawarau Bridge Bungy in advance online — it is extremely popular in November. Minimum weight requirements apply (45kg). Wear comfortable, secure clothing and remove loose items. The experience includes video and photo packages available for purchase.

day_by_day.morning: Take on the Nevis Bungy Jump — New Zealand's highest bungy at 134 metres above the Nevis River gorge. Transfer departs from Queenstown town centre. The jump involves a cable car ride to a suspended pod above the dramatic gorge. The freefall lasts approximately 8.5 seconds — an absolutely unforgettable experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Queenstown by early afternoon. Decompress with a relaxing walk along the Queenstown Bay waterfront or take a scenic TSS Earnslaw steamship cruise on Lake Wakatipu to Walter Peak High Country Farm for a farm tour.
day_by_day.evening: Quiet recovery evening. Enjoy a relaxed dinner and reflect on two incredible bungy experiences. Browse the Queenstown night markets if available (typically Thursday evenings).

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast before the Nevis transfer departs — Queenstown Bakery or your accommodation
meals.lunch: Lunch at Walter Peak Farm on the lake cruise, or back in Queenstown — NZD 25-45
meals.dinner: Pub dinner at Smiths Craft Beer House or Winnies Queenstown — burgers, pizza, craft beers, NZD 25-40 per person

day_by_day.notes: The Nevis Bungy requires booking well in advance and has a minimum weight of 45kg and maximum of 127kg. The transfer from Queenstown takes approximately 45 minutes each way. Doing two bungy jumps on consecutive days is physically and mentally intense — pace yourself. Stay well hydrated.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery day after two big bungy experiences. Sleep in, enjoy a leisurely breakfast, and take a gentle walk along the Queenstown Gardens — a beautiful peninsula park with rose gardens, lawn bowls, and lake views. Low-key and restorative.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Kiwi Birdlife Park in Queenstown to see native New Zealand wildlife including kiwi birds, tuataras, and weka. Alternatively, explore the Queenstown Hill Time Walk — a 2-hour return hike with panoramic views of the basin and surrounding mountains.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a mid-range dinner experience. Consider a cooking class or food tour of Queenstown's Central Otago wine and food scene, or visit a local wine bar to sample Pinot Noir from the Gibbston Valley wine region.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely brunch at a Queenstown cafe — Bespoke Kitchen is excellent for healthy options
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a lakeside cafe — salmon bagel or quinoa salad, NZD 18-28
meals.dinner: Gibbston Valley Winery restaurant (30 min drive) for a wine and food pairing experience, or Fishbone Bar & Grill in Queenstown — NZD 40-55 per person

day_by_day.notes: This is a deliberate rest day built into the itinerary to avoid burnout. November in Queenstown can be warm and sunny — great for gentle outdoor activities. Use this day to do laundry, recharge devices, and plan logistics for the Routeburn Track.

day_by_day.morning: Preparation and travel day for the Routeburn Track Great Walk. Depart Queenstown early and drive approximately 1.5 hours to the Routeburn Track trailhead near Glenorchy. Stop in Glenorchy for supplies and a coffee. Begin the Routeburn Track from the Routeburn Flats end.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike to Routeburn Flats Hut (approximately 2 hours, 7.5km). The trail winds through ancient beech forest along the Routeburn River with stunning mountain views. Arrive at the hut and settle in. This is a DOC Great Walks hut with bunk accommodation and cooking facilities.
day_by_day.evening: Cook dinner at the hut using supplies carried in. Meet fellow trampers from around the world. Enjoy the incredible alpine silence and star-gazing away from city lights. Early night for the big day ahead.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast in Queenstown or Glenorchy before hitting the trail
meals.lunch: Trail lunch eaten on the track — wraps, cheese, crackers, dried fruit, nuts
meals.dinner: Self-cooked hut meal — dehydrated camping meals or pasta with tuna, brought from Queenstown

day_by_day.notes: Routeburn Track Great Walk hut passes must be booked in advance through DOC — they sell out months ahead, especially in November (peak season). Pack all food, a sleeping bag liner, and cooking equipment. Huts have gas cookers, toilets, and cold running water but no showers. Weight pack carefully — aim for under 12kg.

day_by_day.morning: Day 2 on the Routeburn Track. Depart Routeburn Flats Hut early and hike to Routeburn Falls Hut (1 hour, 2.4km). The trail climbs steeply through subalpine terrain with waterfalls and tussock grassland. Routeburn Falls is one of the most spectacular viewpoints on the entire track.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue from Routeburn Falls Hut over Harris Saddle (1,255m) — the highest point of the track with breathtaking 360-degree views of both Fiordland and Mount Aspiring National Parks. Descend to Lake Mackenzie Hut (approximately 4-5 hours total from Routeburn Falls). This is considered the most scenic section of the entire track.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Lake Mackenzie Hut, set in a glacial cirque with a crystal-clear alpine lake. Cook dinner, rest tired legs, and soak in the extraordinary mountain environment. The lake is safe for swimming if you are brave enough.

meals.breakfast: Hut breakfast — oats, instant coffee, dried fruit
meals.lunch: Trail snacks and lunch eaten at Harris Saddle with panoramic views
meals.dinner: Self-cooked hut meal — dehydrated meals or instant noodles with added protein

day_by_day.notes: Harris Saddle can be exposed to strong winds and weather changes even in November. Carry full wet weather gear, warm layers, and sun protection. The views from the saddle on a clear day are among the finest in New Zealand. Check weather forecast the night before at the hut.

day_by_day.morning: Final day on the Routeburn Track. Depart Lake Mackenzie Hut and hike the final section to The Divide on the Milford Road (approximately 3 hours, 9.4km). The trail descends through stunning Fiordland rainforest with ferns, waterfalls, and ancient trees. Arrive at The Divide — the lowest east-west pass in the Southern Alps.
day_by_day.afternoon: Catch the pre-booked shuttle bus from The Divide to Te Anau (approximately 1.5 hours). Check into accommodation in Te Anau — the gateway to Fiordland. Freshen up with a proper shower, do laundry, and rest. Explore Te Anau lakefront in the late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate completing the Routeburn Track Great Walk with a proper sit-down dinner at a Te Anau restaurant. Treat yourself after three days on trail.

meals.breakfast: Final hut breakfast — use up remaining trail food
meals.lunch: Snacks on the final trail section or at The Divide
meals.dinner: The Fat Duck Restaurant in Te Anau — great steaks and seafood, NZD 35-55 per person. Well deserved!

day_by_day.notes: Book the shuttle from The Divide to Te Anau in advance through Tracknet or Alpinecoach — services are timed to connect with hiker arrivals. Confirm your Milford Sound kayak and hike combo booking for the following day. Charge all devices overnight.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Te Anau early for the spectacular 2-hour drive to Milford Sound along one of the world's most scenic roads. Pass through the Homer Tunnel and descend into Fiordland. Begin the Milford Sound Kayak and Hike Combo — start with a guided sea kayak paddle through the majestic fiord, paddling beneath towering waterfalls including Stirling and Lady Bowen Falls.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the combo experience with a guided hike along the Milford foreshore track. Marvel at Mitre Peak rising 1,692 metres directly from the water. The guide will share knowledge of Fiordland ecology, Maori history, and geology. Return kayaks and complete the hike by mid-afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back to Te Anau (2 hours) or Queenstown (4.5 hours) depending on remaining itinerary. Enjoy a quiet dinner and rest after a full day of paddling and hiking.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast in Te Anau before departure — packed if needed
meals.lunch: Packed lunch provided by the kayak tour operator or bring your own snacks
meals.dinner: Redcliff Cafe in Te Anau for New Zealand game meats and local produce — NZD 35-50 per person

day_by_day.notes: Book the Milford Sound Kayak and Hike Combo well in advance — this is one of the most popular activities in Fiordland. Sandflies are notorious at Milford Sound — bring strong insect repellent. November can bring rain to Fiordland which actually enhances the waterfalls dramatically. Dress in layers.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day back toward your base at Aegean Bliss Resort or toward Christchurch for departure. If time allows, stop at Mirror Lakes along the Milford Road for a peaceful morning walk and reflection viewing. Alternatively, visit the Te Anau Glowworm Caves for a magical underground boat tour through glowworm-lit caverns.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue driving north toward Christchurch via the Lindis Pass and Mackenzie Basin. Stop at Lake Pukaki for the iconic turquoise glacier-fed lake views with Aoraki Mount Cook as a backdrop. If energy permits, take the short Mount Cook Village walk or the Tasman Glacier viewpoint track.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive in Christchurch or your final base location. Check in and enjoy a final evening dinner in the city. Explore the Christchurch Botanic Gardens at dusk if arriving early enough.

meals.breakfast: Cafe breakfast in Te Anau before departing
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch at Lake Pukaki with views of Mount Cook — buy supplies in Twizel
meals.dinner: Christchurch restaurant — try Hello Sunday or Gatherings for excellent local cuisine, NZD 35-55 per person

day_by_day.notes: The drive from Te Anau to Christchurch is approximately 6-7 hours with stops. Consider an overnight stop in Twizel or Lake Tekapo to break the journey. Lake Tekapo is a Dark Sky Reserve — incredible stargazing on clear November nights.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in New Zealand South Island. If based in Christchurch, take a morning walk through the beautiful Christchurch Botanic Gardens along the Avon River. Visit the Cardboard Cathedral or explore the Restart Container Mall for last-minute souvenirs and New Zealand gifts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final afternoon activities depending on departure time. Visit the Canterbury Museum (free entry) to learn about South Island history, Antarctic exploration, and Maori culture. Alternatively, take the Christchurch Gondola up to the Port Hills for a final panoramic view over the city, Banks Peninsula, and Southern Alps.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at a Christchurch restaurant celebrating an incredible 13 days on the South Island. Head to the airport for departure or return to Aegean Bliss Resort for a final night.

meals.breakfast: Final New Zealand breakfast — try Harlequin Public House or C1 Espresso in Christchurch for a memorable send-off meal
meals.lunch: Light lunch in the Botanic Gardens cafe or a Christchurch central cafe
meals.dinner: Special farewell dinner at Chillingworth Road or The Peg in Christchurch — celebrate the adventure, NZD 45-65 per person

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before international departure for check-in and security at Christchurch International Airport. Pack any liquid souvenirs such as Manuka honey or wine carefully in checked luggage. New Zealand has strict biosecurity — do not attempt to carry fresh food, seeds, or plant material out of the country. Kia ora and safe travels!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium New Zealand South Island Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, New Zealand South Island

experiences.name: Nevis Bungy Jump
experiences.description: Take the ultimate leap from New Zealand's highest bungy jump at 134 meters above the Nevis River gorge. This iconic AJ Hackett experience offers breathtaking views of the Remarkables mountain range and an adrenaline rush like no other. The jump includes a scenic gondola ride to the suspended pod over the gorge.

experiences.name: Routeburn Track Great Walk
experiences.description: Hike one of New Zealand's nine Great Walks through stunning alpine scenery connecting Fiordland and Mount Aspiring National Parks. The 32km trail features dramatic mountain passes, glacial lakes, and ancient beech forests. Day hikers can tackle the Routeburn Falls section for spectacular views without requiring a multi-day commitment.

experiences.name: Milford Sound Kayak and Hike Combo
experiences.description: Combine a guided sea kayak paddle through the majestic Milford Sound fiord with a short hike along the Milford foreshore track. Paddle beneath towering 1200-meter cliffs, spot fur seals and dolphins, and witness cascading waterfalls up close. This guided full-day experience blends water adventure with light hiking in one of the world's most dramatic landscapes.

experiences.name: Franz Josef Glacier Valley Walk
experiences.description: Hike through a dramatic glacial valley to the terminal face of the Franz Josef Glacier, one of the world's most accessible glaciers. The self-guided valley floor walk winds through ancient rainforest and glacial moraine with interpretive signs explaining the glacier's rapid retreat. For a more immersive experience, join a guided heli-hike to walk on the glacier's icy surface.

experiences.name: Queenstown Ledge Bungy and Swing
experiences.description: Experience the original Kawarau Bridge Bungy, the world's first commercial bungy jump site, where AJ Hackett launched the sport in 1988. Jump 43 meters above the turquoise Kawarau River and optionally get dunked in the water below. The historic site includes a free museum and viewing platform, making it a cultural landmark as well as a thrilling activity.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Travel Day
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - Travel Day
day_by_day.evening: Late arrival at Christchurch or Queenstown Airport at 22:30. Private luxury transfer arranged to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check-in with welcome champagne and light late-night supper prepared by the resort chef.

meals.breakfast: N/A - In-flight
meals.lunch: N/A - In-flight
meals.dinner: Late-night welcome supper at Aegean Bliss Resort - curated cheese board, smoked salmon, artisan breads and a glass of Marlborough Sauvignon Blanc provided upon arrival

day_by_day.notes: Flight lands at 22:30 — no activities scheduled. Ensure private airport transfer is pre-booked. Resort should be notified of late check-in. Unpack minimally and rest well for the adventure ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely resort morning — sleep in and recover from travel. Enjoy a premium à la carte breakfast at the resort's oceanfront restaurant overlooking the beachfront. Take a gentle orientation walk along the beach to acclimatise to the South Island air and scenery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Scenic orientation drive or private guided tour of the surrounding region. Visit a local winery for a premium wine tasting experience — the South Island is renowned for its Pinot Noir and Sauvignon Blanc. Explore the nearby town, browse boutique galleries and artisan shops.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on the resort's beachfront terrace. Indulge in a full spa treatment at the resort spa — deep tissue massage or hot stone therapy to recover from long-haul travel. Early dinner at the resort's signature fine dining restaurant.

meals.breakfast: À la carte breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort — eggs Benedict with smoked salmon, fresh fruit platter, freshly squeezed juices and barista coffee
meals.lunch: Winery platter lunch at a premium local vineyard — artisan cheeses, charcuterie, seasonal produce paired with estate wines
meals.dinner: Signature fine dining at Aegean Bliss Resort — multi-course tasting menu featuring locally sourced South Island ingredients, paired with New Zealand wines

day_by_day.notes: This is a recovery and orientation day. Keep the pace relaxed. Confirm all upcoming activity bookings and transfers with the resort concierge today.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning departure by private luxury vehicle toward Queenstown (approximately 4–5 hours depending on base location). Stop at scenic viewpoints along the way including Lake Tekapo — visit the Church of the Good Shepherd and admire the turquoise glacial lake surrounded by lupins in full November bloom.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Queenstown. Check into a premium day suite or pre-arranged luxury lodge for freshening up. Explore the Queenstown waterfront and lakeside promenade. Browse Queenstown's upscale boutiques along The Mall. Optional: private e-bike tour along the Queenstown Trail.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cruise on Lake Wakatipu aboard a private chartered vessel with champagne and canapés. Dinner at Queenstown's finest restaurant — Amisfield Winery Bistro or Rata by Josh Emett, featuring farm-to-table South Island cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort before departure — eggs your way, smashed avocado, house-baked sourdough, cold brew coffee
meals.lunch: Lakeside lunch at Queenstown's Pier 19 or The Bathhouse — fresh South Island salmon, green-lipped mussels and local craft beer or wine
meals.dinner: Fine dining at Rata by Josh Emett — seasonal degustation menu showcasing Central Otago produce with matched New Zealand wine flight

day_by_day.notes: Depart resort early (by 7:30am) to allow scenic stops at Lake Tekapo. Pre-book dinner reservation at Rata well in advance as it fills quickly. Private transfer recommended for this drive.

day_by_day.morning: Queenstown Ledge Bungy and Swing — Experience the iconic Kawarau Bridge Bungy, the world's first commercial bungy jump site at 43 metres above the turquoise Kawarau River. Watch others leap before taking your own plunge. This legendary AJ Hackett site includes a private viewing platform and premium bungy package with video and photos.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the adrenaline rush, enjoy a leisurely lunch then take the Skyline Gondola to the top of Bob's Peak for panoramic views over Queenstown and Lake Wakatipu. Try the luge track or simply enjoy the views. Optional: paragliding tandem flight over Queenstown for continued adventure.
day_by_day.evening: Premium spa recovery session at your Queenstown luxury accommodation. Dinner at Botswana Butchery or Amisfield Winery — celebrated for its exceptional Central Otago Pinot Noir and seasonal tasting menus.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at your Queenstown luxury lodge — avocado toast, house-cured gravlax, seasonal berries, specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Post-bungy celebratory lunch at Stratosfare Restaurant at the top of Skyline Gondola — buffet with panoramic views over Queenstown
meals.dinner: Dinner at Botswana Butchery Queenstown — premium South Island lamb rack, dry-aged beef, Central Otago wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Book Kawarau Bungy in advance through AJ Hackett. The Ledge Bungy (47m) is also available in Queenstown if you prefer an urban bungy experience with night options. Wear comfortable, secure clothing and closed-toe shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Nevis Bungy Jump — Take the ultimate leap from New Zealand's highest bungy at 134 metres above the dramatic Nevis River gorge. Transfer via 4WD to the remote site, then step into the suspended cable car pod and plunge into the abyss. The most extreme bungy experience in New Zealand — a true bucket-list moment.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the Nevis experience, decompress with a scenic helicopter flight over the Remarkables mountain range and surrounding Central Otago landscapes. Land on a remote alpine peak for a champagne toast with breathtaking 360-degree views.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Queenstown. Relax with a private in-room couples massage or solo deep tissue treatment. Enjoy a leisurely fine dining dinner celebrating your extraordinary day of adventure.

meals.breakfast: Light but energising breakfast before the Nevis jump — fresh fruit, muesli, poached eggs on toast, green juice at your lodge
meals.lunch: Post-jump gourmet picnic hamper prepared by your lodge — artisan sandwiches, local cheeses, seasonal fruit, sparkling water and juice
meals.dinner: Degustation dinner at Amisfield Winery Bistro — 'Trust the Chef' seasonal menu with matched Central Otago wines in a stunning vineyard setting

day_by_day.notes: The Nevis Bungy requires advance booking with AJ Hackett. Weight restrictions apply (45–127kg). Transfer departs Queenstown town centre. Allow full morning for the experience including travel time. This is the most thrilling day of the trip — capture it all on the included GoPro package.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Queenstown early for the spectacular drive to Te Anau (approximately 2.5 hours) — gateway to Fiordland National Park. Stop at the Kingston Flyer historic train site and enjoy views over Lake Wakatipu. Arrive in Te Anau and check into a premium lakeside lodge.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Te Anau township and the shores of Lake Te Anau, New Zealand's largest South Island lake. Visit the Te Anau Glowworm Caves by private boat — a magical underground world of ancient limestone and thousands of glowworms illuminating the cave ceiling.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset walk along the Te Anau lakefront. Dinner at a premium Te Anau restaurant — fresh Fiordland venison, blue cod and local produce. Early night in preparation for the Routeburn Track tomorrow.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at Queenstown lodge before departure — full cooked breakfast with fresh juices and barista coffee
meals.lunch: Lakeside lunch at Te Anau's Sandfly Café or The Fat Duck — venison burger, blue cod fish and chips, local craft beer
meals.dinner: Fine dining at Redcliff Restaurant Te Anau — Fiordland venison, wild boar and seasonal local produce in a cosy heritage cottage setting

day_by_day.notes: Book Te Anau Glowworm Caves in advance — evening tours are particularly atmospheric. Prepare hiking gear for the Routeburn Track tomorrow. Check weather forecast for Fiordland — November is generally excellent but rain is always possible.

day_by_day.morning: Routeburn Track Great Walk — Day 1. Depart Te Anau by private transfer to the Routeburn Shelter trailhead (1.5 hours). Begin the iconic Routeburn Track, one of New Zealand's nine Great Walks. Hike through ancient beech forests and along crystal-clear mountain streams toward Routeburn Flats (2 hours, 7.5km). Arrive at the premium Routeburn Flats Hut for lunch.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue hiking from Routeburn Flats to Routeburn Falls Hut (1.5 hours, 2.5km). Ascend through increasingly dramatic alpine scenery with cascading waterfalls. Arrive at Routeburn Falls Hut perched at 1,000m elevation with extraordinary mountain views. Explore the surroundings, spot kea parrots and take in the alpine wilderness.
day_by_day.evening: Settle into Routeburn Falls Hut (premium Great Walk hut with cooking facilities and comfortable bunks). Prepare a hot dinner using pre-packed premium provisions supplied by your luxury outfitter. Star gazing from the hut deck — Fiordland's dark skies offer extraordinary views of the Milky Way.

meals.breakfast: Packed gourmet breakfast box from Te Anau lodge — muesli, energy bars, fresh fruit, thermos of coffee
meals.lunch: Gourmet trail lunch at Routeburn Flats Hut — premium deli wraps, hard cheeses, charcuterie, nuts, dried fruit and chocolate
meals.dinner: Premium self-catered hut dinner — freeze-dried gourmet meals (pre-arranged with luxury outfitter) plus wine in lightweight pouches, chocolate dessert

day_by_day.notes: Book Routeburn Track Great Walk hut passes well in advance through DOC — these sell out quickly, especially in November (peak season). A guided luxury Routeburn experience with Ultimate Hikes is highly recommended — they provide all meals, gear and guiding. Pack rain gear, layers and sturdy hiking boots.

day_by_day.morning: Routeburn Track Great Walk — Day 2. Early morning start from Routeburn Falls Hut. Ascend to Harris Saddle (1,255m) — the highest point of the track with panoramic views across Fiordland and Mount Aspiring National Parks on a clear day. Optional side trip to Conical Hill summit (30 min return) for even more spectacular 360-degree alpine views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend from Harris Saddle through the stunning Lake Mackenzie basin. Arrive at Lake Mackenzie Hut for lunch beside the impossibly blue alpine lake. Continue hiking to the Divide (end of track, 4 hours total from Harris Saddle). Private transfer arranged back to Te Anau or onward to Milford Sound.
day_by_day.evening: Check into premium Milford Sound Lodge — the only accommodation within the Milford Sound valley. Enjoy a well-earned hot shower and premium dinner at the lodge restaurant. Reflect on two extraordinary days on the Routeburn Track.

meals.breakfast: Hot porridge with honey and nuts, energy bars and coffee at Routeburn Falls Hut before departure
meals.lunch: Packed trail lunch at Lake Mackenzie Hut — gourmet wraps, premium snacks, energy gels and hot tea from thermos
meals.dinner: Dinner at Milford Sound Lodge restaurant — pan-seared blue cod, Fiordland venison, local craft beer and Central Otago wine

day_by_day.notes: The Routeburn Track in its entirety is 32km over 2–3 days. This itinerary covers the most spectacular sections. Weather at Harris Saddle can change rapidly — always carry full rain gear. Helicopter evacuation is available if weather closes in. Confirm private transfer from The Divide to Milford Sound.

day_by_day.morning: Milford Sound Kayak and Hike Combo — Begin with a guided sea kayak paddle through the majestic Milford Sound fiord at dawn, when the Sound is at its most serene and mist-draped. Paddle beneath the towering 1,692m Mitre Peak, past cascading Stirling and Lady Bowen Falls, and through the mirror-calm waters of this UNESCO World Heritage fiord.
day_by_day.afternoon: After kayaking, join a short guided hike along the Milford foreshore track and into the surrounding rainforest. Spot Fiordland crested penguins, fur seals and bottlenose dolphins. Board a premium small-group cruise on Milford Sound for lunch, venturing to the Tasman Sea heads for maximum wildlife viewing.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Milford Sound Lodge. Sunset photography session at the Sound — November light at Milford is extraordinary, with long golden hours. Premium dinner at the lodge with a glass of Marlborough Pinot Gris watching the last light fade over the fiord walls.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at Milford Sound Lodge before kayaking — muesli, yoghurt, fruit, coffee (kayak tours depart at dawn)
meals.lunch: Premium catered lunch aboard the Milford Sound cruise — fresh sandwiches, salads, hot soup and beverages with fiord views
meals.dinner: Fine dining at Milford Sound Lodge — Fiordland crayfish, venison loin, seasonal vegetables, Marlborough wine selection

day_by_day.notes: Book the kayak and hike combo with Rosco's Milford Kayaks or Go Orange — small group premium options available. Dawn paddles are magical but require early wake-up (5:30am). Bring waterproof layers for kayaking. Sandflies are notorious at Milford — bring strong insect repellent.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Milford Sound and drive the spectacular Milford Road back toward Te Anau. Stop at the Mirror Lakes, Eglinton Valley and the Homer Tunnel for photography. Continue driving north toward the West Coast, crossing through the Southern Alps via Haast Pass — one of the world's most scenic drives.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Franz Josef Glacier township on the West Coast (approximately 5–6 hours total driving). Check into a premium West Coast lodge or boutique hotel. Rest and freshen up. Optional: short walk to the Franz Josef Glacier viewpoint for your first glimpse of the ancient ice.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Franz Josef village. Enjoy a hot pool soak at Glacier Hot Pools — outdoor thermal pools surrounded by rainforest with views toward the glacier. Dinner at the Alice May Restaurant or a premium lodge dining room.

meals.breakfast: Packed breakfast from Milford Sound Lodge for the road — pastries, fruit, coffee in a thermos
meals.lunch: Scenic picnic lunch at a Haast Pass viewpoint — premium hamper prepared by your lodge with gourmet sandwiches, local cheeses and wine
meals.dinner: Dinner at Alice May Restaurant Franz Josef — West Coast whitebait fritters, venison, locally sourced produce and New Zealand craft beer

day_by_day.notes: This is a long driving day — depart Milford Sound by 8:00am. The Haast Pass drive is one of the world's great scenic drives — allow time for stops. November weather on the West Coast can be wet — pack rain gear. Book Glacier Hot Pools in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Franz Josef Glacier Valley Walk — Hike through the dramatic glacial valley to the terminal face of Franz Josef Glacier, one of the world's most accessible glaciers. Walk through ancient rainforest that gives way to a raw glacial landscape of grey moraine and ice-cold meltwater streams. The terminal face reveals towering blue-white ice walls — a humbling natural spectacle.
day_by_day.afternoon: Heli-hike on Franz Josef Glacier — for the ultimate premium experience, take a scenic helicopter flight onto the upper glacier snowfields and hike across ancient blue ice with a certified guide. Explore ice caves, crevasses and seracs in a remote alpine wilderness accessible only by air. This is one of New Zealand's most exclusive experiences.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Franz Josef village. Celebrate an extraordinary day with a premium dinner. Optional: guided glow-worm dell walk through the rainforest after dark — thousands of glow-worms illuminate the forest floor just minutes from the village.

meals.breakfast: Full cooked breakfast at your Franz Josef lodge — eggs Benedict, smoked salmon, fresh fruit, specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Light packed lunch on the glacier — energy bars, fruit, nuts and thermos of hot soup (provided by heli-hike operator)
meals.dinner: Premium dinner at your lodge's restaurant or The Landing Bar & Restaurant — West Coast lamb, fresh seafood, Central Otago wine

day_by_day.notes: Book the Franz Josef heli-hike with Franz Josef Glacier Guides well in advance — weather cancellations are common on the West Coast. Always have a flexible backup day planned. The valley walk is free and self-guided but guided options are available. Wear sturdy waterproof boots and warm layers — the glacier valley is significantly colder than the village.

day_by_day.morning: Scenic morning drive from Franz Josef south toward Wanaka (approximately 4 hours via Haast). Stop at the stunning Blue Pools in the Haast Pass — a short 30-minute return walk through ancient kahikatea forest to crystal-clear blue swimming holes. Continue to Wanaka, arriving late morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Wanaka township — visit the iconic 'That Wanaka Tree' for photographs, kayak on Lake Wanaka or take a stand-up paddleboard lesson on the glassy lake. Visit Rippon Vineyard for a premium wine tasting overlooking the lake and the Crown Range — one of the most beautiful vineyard settings in the world.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset at Lake Wanaka — the November light here is extraordinary with long golden hours. Dinner at Wanaka's finest restaurant — Francesca's Italian Kitchen or Kika for contemporary New Zealand cuisine. Final night in the South Island's interior before returning to base.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at Franz Josef lodge before departure — full cooked breakfast with fresh juices
meals.lunch: Lakeside lunch at Wanaka's Ritual Café or Francesca's — fresh salads, artisan pizzas, local craft beer
meals.dinner: Fine dining at Kika Wanaka — seasonal sharing plates featuring Central Otago produce, matched with local wines in a sophisticated lakeside setting

day_by_day.notes: The Blue Pools walk is a must-stop on the Haast Pass — allow 45 minutes. Arrive in Wanaka before noon to maximise the afternoon. Wanaka is a beautiful, quieter alternative to Queenstown. Book Rippon Vineyard tasting in advance — they have limited capacity.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Wanaka — sunrise walk to Roys Peak Lookout (optional, departs 5:30am for the famous summit sunrise view, 2 hours return to viewpoint). Alternatively, a leisurely final breakfast and a gentle lakeside walk. Visit the Puzzling World attraction or simply savour the last views of Lake Wanaka and the Southern Alps.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depart Wanaka and drive back toward your resort base or onward to Christchurch or Queenstown for departure flights. Final scenic stops along the Crown Range Road — the highest sealed road in New Zealand with spectacular views over the Cardrona Valley. Return to Aegean Bliss Resort for final night or transfer to departure airport.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at the finest restaurant near your final location — a celebration of an extraordinary 13-day South Island adventure. Toast to the Nevis leap, the Routeburn ridgelines, Milford Sound at dawn and the Franz Josef ice. Reflect on an unforgettable premium New Zealand experience.

meals.breakfast: Final gourmet breakfast in Wanaka — eggs your way, smashed avocado, sourdough, fresh juices and excellent coffee at a lakeside café
meals.lunch: Scenic lunch stop at Cardrona Hotel (1863) — one of New Zealand's most historic pubs, serving hearty lunches with craft beer in a charming gold rush setting
meals.dinner: Farewell fine dining dinner — if returning to resort base, the Aegean Bliss Resort signature restaurant for a final multi-course tasting menu; if at Queenstown, Amisfield Winery for a memorable final evening

day_by_day.notes: Confirm departure flight times and arrange private airport transfers well in advance. Allow extra time at the airport — New Zealand domestic and international check-in requires 90 minutes minimum. Pack any New Zealand wine, manuka honey or artisan food souvenirs carefully in checked luggage. This has been an extraordinary 13-day premium adventure through the South Island's most iconic landscapes and adrenaline experiences.
